etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English quiete, from Old French quiet (adjective) and quiete (noun), from Latin quiētus, past participle of quiēscere (“to keep quiet, rest”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷyeh₁- (“rest”). Doublet of coy, quit, and quietus.

definitions.definition: With little or no sound; free of disturbing noise.

quote.text: On the light streets, better streetcleaners, more trees, more police, and quieter buses were the most popular improvements, followed by cutting down the number of cars and improving children's play space.

quote.citation: 1999 April 5, William Safire, “Essay; The Quiet Noisemaker”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Before long, the unsuspecting salesman was earnestly pitching him "the quietest noisemaker on the market."

definitions.definition: Having little motion or activity; calm.

quote.citation: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 8, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:
quote.text: It was a casual sneer, obviously one of a long line. There was hatred behind it, but of a quiet, chronic type, nothing new or unduly virulent, and he was taken aback by the flicker of amazed incredulity that passed over the younger man's ravaged face.

definitions.definition: Not talking much or not talking loudly; reserved.
(transitive) To cause (someone or something) to become quiet.

quote.citation: 1631, Saint Augustine, “He Admires Gods Majesty, and is Inflamed with a Deepe Desire of Praising Him”, in William Watts, transl., Saint Augustines Confessions Translated: […], London:  […]  Iohn Norton, for Iohn Partridge […], →OCLC, book 1, paragraph 1, page 2:
quote.text: For thou haſt created us for thy ſelfe, and our heart cannot be quieted till it may fine repoſe in thee.

definitions.definition: The absence of movement; stillness, tranquility.
The absence of disturbance or trouble; peace, security.

quote.citation: 1593, anonymous author, The Life and Death of Iacke Straw […], Act III:
quote.text: The King & his Nobles thinke they may ſleepe in quiet,Now they haue giuen vs a little holy water at the Court,But thers no ſuch matter, we be no ſuch fooles,To be bobd out with words and after come to hanging:  […]
